module_summary: src/init.c owns the IOP module lifecycle of the EE program: it holds the have_* residency flags for every embedded IRX, loads driver stacks lazily on first device access (DEV9/network/SMB/NFS/UDPFS, HDD/ATA/DVR, USB/BDM, MMCE, MX4SIO, iLink, PC CARD CF, xfrom, keyboard, HDL info), switches mutually exclusive stacks by rebooting the IOP (resetRuntimeDeviceState/Reset), and provides the special reboots for the MagicGate signer IOPRP and the Ember USB keep-IOP handoff. It also contains the bounded fileXio GETSTAT RPC client, the power-off callback, the SMB server start/stop devctls and the dashboard DNS setup. include/kelf_signer.h only declares the three KELF signer entry points implemented in src/kelf_signer.c.

reusable_helpers.name: fileXioGetStatBounded
reusable_helpers.what: fileXio GETSTAT through a private NOWAIT RPC client with a millisecond deadline, so a wedged device cannot freeze the caller

reusable_helpers.name: waitForUsbMassPath
reusable_helpers.what: polls a USB path with bounded stats until it answers or a 2 s deadline passes

reusable_helpers.name: loadExternalFile
reusable_helpers.what: reads a whole file from any device into a 64-byte aligned malloc buffer, returns size

reusable_helpers.name: isPathDeviceStackLoaded
reusable_helpers.what: tells whether a device path can be accessed without loading a driver or rebooting the IOP

reusable_helpers.name: setFileXioTransferWide
reusable_helpers.what: switches the fileXio IOP transfer buffer between 128/64/16 KB with fallback

findings.title: HDL info RPC stays 'ready' across IOP resets and after a failed load: HDD manager calls SifCallRpc on a stale or unbound client
findings.problem: Hdl_Inited (hdl_rpc.c:24,48) is set once and never cleared: clearIopModuleState only clears have_hdl_info (init.c:2998). After any IOP reset (stack switch MMCE/MX4SIO/UDPFS, mc1 with MX4SIO, DEV9 family change), dash_hdd hdlReady returns 1 without reloading hdl_info.irx and HdlGetGameInfo/HdlRenameGame issue blocking SifCallRpc through a client bound to the previous IOP session. Also loadHdlInfoModule ignores ID/ret and the bind result; when the module did not start, Hdl_Info_BindRpc spins 0x1000 binds x 0x10000 nop loops and still sets Hdl_Inited=1, so the call goes to a NULL server.
findings.fix: Clear Hdl_Inited in clearIopModuleState next to have_hdl_info; in loadHdlInfoModule skip the bind when ID < 0 or ret == 1; in Hdl_Info_BindRpc set Hdl_Inited only when client.server != 0; key dash_hdd's one-shot 'tried' to getIopResetGeneration() so the module is reloaded once per IOP session.
findings.justification: The checks replace an unconditional 'ready' latch that lets a blocking RPC reach a dead or absent IOP server (console freeze, INFERRED). Each is one condition on existing state; no new mechanism is added.
findings.benefit: Removes a likely hard freeze when the HDD manager is reopened after any IOP reset, and a ~3-5 s UI-thread spin when hdl_info fails (INFERRED: 2^28 loop iterations of 4 nops at 294.9 MHz plus 4096 bind round trips).
findings.evidence: Read init.c:2563-2574, 2965-3040; hdl_rpc.c:1-84; dash_hdd.c:419-449. grep Hdl_Inited over src: only hdl_rpc.c:24 (def), :48 (set), :57/:74 (checks), dash_hdd.c:419/425/436; nothing clears it. grep have_hdl_info: init.c:182, 2567, 2572, 2998 only. Callers: loadHdlInfoModule only from dash_hdd.c:434; HdlGetGameInfo dash_hdd.c:448 (UI), HdlRenameGame dash_hdd.c:281 (worker job). hdl_info imports atad/dev9/PoweroffShutdown (iop/hdl_info/imports.lst:2-47), so a missing dependency makes the load fail. INFERRED part: IOP sifrpc behaviour when the call carries a stale or NULL server pointer (SDK source not in repo).

findings.title: prepareExploitSignerIop reboots the IOP without the teardown resetRuntimeDeviceState requires (FTP close, PAD close, mc poll drain, sound)
findings.problem: The exploit installer's signer reboot (init.c:838-874) only stops SMB/PCCF, closes the keyboard and unmounts. It skips what the file's own reset path documents as required: ftpSessionShutdown refusal (2172-2177; an FTP upload to the card is cut by the reboot), filerRootMcPollIdle (2182-2186; pending mcGetInfo leaves the pad dark), padPortClose/padEnd before setupPad (2197-2205; 'UI alive, controller dead'), dashSoundShutdown (2189-2193). The installer then needs pad input and writes to the card.
findings.fix: Run the signer reboot through the same path as every other reset: let Reset() take an optional IOPRP buffer (NULL = SifIopReset) and have prepareExploitSignerIop call resetRuntimeDeviceState with it, then check have_exploit_signer_iop/generation for a refused reset. This deletes the duplicated reboot/reload sequence at 845-874.
findings.benefit: Closes a card-corruption window (FTP write cut mid-file) and an intermittent dead-controller state after the signer reboot; ~25 duplicated reset lines removed (INFERRED from 845-874 vs 3053-3093).
findings.evidence: Read init.c:821-882, 2163-2221, 3048-3098; main_exploit_installer.c:1053-1057 and call sites 1963, 2289 (install flows that then write the card and show dialogs). ftp_session.c:70-83 ftpSessionShutdown closes FTP sessions before a reset; prepareExploitSignerIop never calls it (grep ftpSession in main_exploit_installer.c: none). dash_worker.c:153-164 iopResetHook is a no-op on the UI thread, so the missing iopResetNotify is harmless. pad.c:428-452 reopenPadPorts documents the stale-libpad failure. INFERRED part: that the stale pad and pending libmc request actually fail on this specific reboot (intermittent per the repo's own comments).

findings.title: Power-button handler is lost when load_ps2dev9 reboots the IOP after the caller armed it, and is never armed in USB-only sessions
findings.problem: Each DEV9 loader calls setupPowerOff() and then reaches load_ps2dev9, which reboots the IOP when the Legacy Ethernet setting was toggled (dash_settings.c:1905 changes it live). Reset clears have_poweroff and done_setupPowerOff (3001, 3024) and nothing re-arms them, so the new HDD/ATA/network stack runs without poweroff.irx: a power-button press skips PFS CLOSEALL, HDD idle and DEV9 off. USB, MMCE, MX4SIO and iLink loaders never call setupPowerOff, so the USB STOP UNIT at 2614-2615 never runs from the button in those sessions.
findings.fix: Call setupPowerOff() once inside load_ps2dev9 after the variant-switch reset and before DEV9 is executed, and delete the seven caller calls at 921, 967, 1024, 2551, 2677, 2701, 2723 (all reach load_ps2dev9). Add the same single call in loadUsbModules if USB HDD STOP UNIT on the button is wanted.
findings.justification: Moving the call to the one place every DEV9 path passes after any reset fixes the ordering bug and removes six call sites; the optional USB call is one line for the documented emergency-park problem.
findings.benefit: Power-button shutdown again flushes HDD/PFS after a DEV9 family switch and stops USB disks; ~6 call lines removed (READ: 7 removed, 1 added).
findings.evidence: Read init.c:487-523, 908-990, 1010-1054, 2531-2558, 2637-2734, 2965-3098, 1740-1817. grep setupPowerOff() over src: init.c 921, 967, 1024, 2493, 2551, 2677, 2701, 2723 and main_actions.c:759 (explicit menu) only; no call in Reset, ensureCoreIoStackReady, loadUsbModules, boot code. grep legacy_net_drivers: set live at dash_settings.c:1905 with no reset; read at init.c:496 and 951. INFERRED part: what the console does on a power-button press when poweroff.irx is not resident (no callback, so closeAllAndPoweroff does not run).

findings.title: Fixed sleep(1) on the UI thread after every ATA_BD load (HDD/ATA boot, first hdd0:/ata0: access, after each IOP reset)
findings.problem: loadAtaBlockDriver sleeps 1 s after ATA_BD starts. In EXFAT builds both loadAtaModules and loadHddModules (load_ps2hdd_stack(1)) go through it, from the dashboard device probe and the HDD/ATA boot path on the UI thread, so the screen stops for a full second once per IOP session. The ata0: probe that follows already waits up to 2000 ms for the device (dash_devices.c:611), and RiptOPL loads ATAD and its HDD modules back to back with no pause (src/sources/hddsupport.cpp:654-658).
findings.fix: Delete pauseAfterAtaBlockDriverLoad and its call; rely on the driver's own device init and the existing bounded probe. Verify HDD/ATA detection on hardware.
findings.benefit: 1000 ms less UI freeze on HDD/ATA boot and on first HDD/ATA access per IOP session (INFERRED from sleep(1)); ~7 lines removed.
findings.evidence: Read init.c:683-744, 2500-2558, 2663-2688; dash_devices.c:594-611 (probeMount on UI thread, ata probe 2000 ms); main_startup.c:651-658 (boot device ATA/HDD). git log -S pauseAfterAtaBlockDriverLoad: only the initial import 944a2fc, no recorded hardware reason. Cross-repo: RiptOPL src/sources/hddsupport.cpp:654-658 loads ATAD then XHDD without a delay. INFERRED part: that no drive needs the settle window (needs hardware test).

findings.title: getExternalFilePath dereferences NULL for an hdd0:/PART or dvr_hdd0:/PART path without a file part (boot-time crash from a hand-edited CNF)
findings.problem: For 'hdd0:/NAME' the code builds party='hdd0:NAME', then p=strchr(party,'/') is NULL, so sprintf prints '(null)' and *p=0 stores to address 0; the DVR branch is identical. USBKBD_FILE and KBDMAP_FILE are copied from the CNF unchecked (config.c:1039-1042) and startKbd runs on every boot, safe mode included (main_modules.c:54), so such a value crashes each start until the CNF is fixed elsewhere. Paths picked in the file browser always contain the file part.
findings.fix: When p is NULL, fall back to genFixPath(argPath, filePath) and return (one check per branch).
findings.justification: One NULL test per branch closes a store to address 0 reached from a config value at boot; nothing simpler prevents it.
findings.benefit: Removes a boot crash loop on a malformed keyboard path (INFERRED consequence of a NULL store on the EE).
findings.evidence: Read init.c:1412-1463, 1533-1556, 2108-2119, 2919-2953; config.c:1039-1042; main_modules.c:18-59. grep usbkbd_file|kbdmap_file: set by config.c:1040/1042, config_startup.c:160/162 (file browser), dash_settings.c:2041/2044 (file picker); read only by init.c loadKbdModules/startKbd. Callers of getExternalFilePath: loadExternalFile and loadExternalModule only.

findings.title: loadExternalModule reports a failed embedded load as success (raw module ID used as a flag)
findings.problem: def_OK holds the return of SifExecModuleBuffer, which is negative on failure, so 'if (def_OK) return 1' also returns 1 when the embedded ps2kbd/DS34 module failed to load (and the start result in dummy is ignored). have_ps2kbd or have_ds34 is then latched for the IOP session, startKbd marks the keyboard open, and no retry happens; the header comment at 1523-1531 promises 0 in that case.
findings.fix: Set def_OK to (ID >= 0 && dummy != 1) instead of the raw ID.
findings.benefit: Correct 'not loaded' result for the keyboard/DS34 fallback; one-line change, no size change.
findings.evidence: Read init.c:1523-1556 and both callers (loadDs34Modules 1716-1723, loadKbdModules 2108-2119); grep loadExternalModule over src: definition, prototype at 360 and these three calls only. Elsewhere the file treats ID < 0 or ret == 1 (MODULE_NO_RESIDENT_END) as failure (comments at 641, 1192, 2899).
